lines.text: What if anyone could teleport, anywhere on Earth, in a blink?
Just picture a place, and you're there.
Day one. Your commute drops to zero.
The morning traffic jam simply melts away.
Week one. Airlines carry around five billion passengers a year. Suddenly, almost nobody needs a plane.
Airlines, taxis and car makers scramble to survive.

segments.caption: Empty roads
segments.fact: ROAD CRASHES: ~1.19 MILLION DEATHS A YEAR

lines.text: Month one. Road crashes kill about one point two million people a year.
With far fewer cars on the road, that number could drop sharply.
Transport makes about a quarter of the world's carbon emissions from energy, and much of it comes from carrying people.
As those trips vanish, city air starts to clear.
Year one. You can live by a quiet beach and still pop into the office every morning.
Remote places suddenly become prime real estate.
Borders, banks and bedrooms all need protection from surprise visitors.
So, where would you teleport first?
